extracted.intended_audience: prospective grant applicants, research administrators, and policy analysts interested in NSF-funded college‑teacher education programs
extracted.subtask_description: A scanned/OCR listing/catalog of funded projects (NSF style) focused on college‑teacher instructional development and science education support, showing project titles, institutions, PIs, program labels, durations, and award amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: RESEARCH PARTS FOR COLLEGE TCHRS-ACAD. YR. PHASE
rubrics_metrics.description: Project type repeatedly listed as 'RESEARCH PARTS FOR COLLEGE TCHRS- ACAD. YR. PHASE'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples on page: typically shown as '24 MONTHS $2,000' (many entries such as SCHRECK, JAMES O; STEINMETZ JR, CHARLES; etc.). Indicates an academic‑year phase research grant line item, often 24 months and $2,000 in these listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: SUMMER ISSTITUTE / SUMMER INSTITUTE (FOR COLLEGE TEACHERS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects labeled as 'SUMMER ISSTiTUTE' or 'SUMMER ISSTITVTE ... FOR COLLEGE TEACHERS' (discipline‑specific summer institutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'SUMMER ISSTITUTE IS TROPICAL BOTANY FOR COLLEGE TEACHERS {Y00947E}; 12 MONTHS $59,132' and many others (typically 12 months listed, award sizes vary widely).

rubrics_metrics.name: SHORT COURSE (FOR COLLEGE TEACHERS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects labeled 'SHORT COURSE ... FOR COLLEGE TEACHERS' (discipline or method short courses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'SHORT COURSE IS SOCIAL SCIENCE METHODS', 'SHORT COURSE IS DIGITAL AND ANALOG ELECTRONICS FOR COLLEGE TEACHERS', typically listed with '12 MONTHS' and varying award amounts (e.g., $48,064, $76,034).

rubrics_metrics.name: INSTRUCTIONAL PERSONNEL DEVELOPMENT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as a program umbrella under which many projects (research parts, institutes, short courses) are categorized on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: SCIENCE EDUCATION SUPPORT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another umbrella program grouping many cooperative programs, centers, and curriculum development awards (appears multiple times in the listing).

rubrics_metrics.name: INSTRUCTIONAL PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists cooperative college‑school projects, leadership preparation, curriculum implementation, and related development awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: COOPERATIVE COLLEGE‑SCHOOL SCIENCE (COOPERATIVE PROGRAMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects described as 'COOPERATIVE COLLEGE SCHOOL SCIESCE' or 'COOPERATIVE COLLEGE‑SCHOOL SCIENCE'—partnerships between colleges and K–12 schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: often duration ~19–20 months and award amounts shown (e.g., '19 MONTHS $27,362', '20 MONTHS $32,151'). Represents a consistent project modality on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEADERSHIP PREP FOR IMPLEMENTATIONS / LEADERSHIP PREPARATIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects described as 'LEADERSHIP PREP F IMPL E MESTATIOS' / 'LEADERSHIP PREPARATIOS FOR IMPLEMENTATIONS' (leadership preparation for curriculum implementation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: frequently '18 MONTHS' and amounts like $28,100, $31,900; used for preparing supervisors/administrators for curriculum or program implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHASE / TIMING LABELS: 'ACAD. YR. PHASE' vs 'SUMMER PHASE'
rubrics_metrics.description: Project entries explicitly indicate a program phase such as 'ACAD. YR. PHASE' (academic‑year) or summer institute phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to distinguish timing/operational phase of awards (affects duration and typical award size). Many 'RESEARCH PARTS' entries include 'ACAD. YR. PHASE'; many institutes/short courses are summer phase and listed as '12 MONTHS'.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRAVEL / INTERNATIONAL PARTICIPANT SUPPORT
rubrics_metrics.description: Line items for travel support of international participants (e.g., 'TRAVEL OF ASIAs PARTICIPANTS TO NSF ... TRAINING PROGRAMS').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'TRAVEL OF ASIAS PARTtCiPASTS TO NSF SVMS...TRALSISO PROGRAMS', with durations/amounts provided. Indicates a project type supporting participant travel to NSF workshops/programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: CENTER / CENTER OF EXCELLENCE (SCIENCE EDUCATION CENTER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Larger institutional projects labeled as a 'CENTER' or 'CENTER OF EXCELLENCE' in science education or related areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'CENTER OF EXCELLESCE IS SCIENCE EDUCA- TIOS' appears (Portis, Alan M; 'CENTER OF EXCELLENCE IS SCIENCE EDUCATION' type projects), typically larger dollar amounts (e.g., $143,000).

rubrics_metrics.name: COMPUTER‑BASED / SELF‑INSTRUCTIONAL COURSES
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects described as 'COMPUTER-BASED SELF‑INSTRUCTIONAL COURSE' or other computer‑aided instructional developments for teacher training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: 'COMPUTERBASED SELF INSTRUCTIONAL COURSE FOR SUPPLEMENTARY TRAINING OF SECONDARY SCHOOL TEACHERS OF PHYSICS ... 3 MONTHS $6,300'. These entries specify modality and a sample budget/duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: DISCIPLINE‑SPECIFIC TOPICS (project topicality)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project titles are discipline‑specific (e.g., tropical botany, experimental psychology, solid state, spectroscopy, microeconomic theory applied to public policy, tropical botany, etc.), indicating topical focus is a key attribute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many entries explicitly include the subject area in the project title, showing topical relevance is essential in categorizing and describing awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: TYPICAL DURATION AND AWARD SIZE RANGES
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit standard metrics: durations commonly 12 months (summer institutes/short courses), 24 months (academic‑year research parts), ~19–20 months (cooperative programs), with award amounts varying by project type (research parts often $2,000; institutes/centers much larger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples across page: '24 MONTHS $2,000' repeated for many 'RESEARCH PARTS'; '12 MONTHS $59,132' for a summer institute; '19 MONTHS $27,362' for cooperative programs; 'CENTER' awards show larger sums (>$100,000). These illustrate expected scale/duration by program type on this listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: TARGET AUDIENCE: COLLEGE TEACHERS
rubrics_metrics.description: Most projects explicitly target 'COLLEGE TEACHERS' (in titles and program descriptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every project line repeatedly states the beneficiary audience (e.g., 'FOR COLLEGE TEACHERS'), indicating that audience specification is a primary organizing attribute of these awards.
